/-- `F_{k,m}` for `m = 4 ^ t`: `ℓ = log₂ m = 2t` and `r = ⌈20 log₂ m⌉ = 40t`.
`C` stays a parameter because the preprint specifies a construction scheme, not
one gate numbering. Family theorems quantify over circuits realising `P`. -/
noncomputable def Fkm (k t : ℕ) (C : Circuit (ForrelationCoord k t)) :
    TotalBool (BitLoc (2 * t) (40 * t) C.size (ForrelationCoord k t)) :=
  addressedF (P k t) C (2 * t) (40 * t)

/-- Equation (4) with `δ = 2^(-5k)`, written as the exact integer tests of
Lemma 2.1(iii). A large negative value of `Φ` is outside the promise. -/
def P (k t : ℕ) : PartialBool (ForrelationCoord k t) := fun z =>
  let N := forrelationNumerator k t z
  let M := forrelationDenominator k t
  if (2 : ℤ) ^ (5 * k) * N ≥ M then some true
  else if (2 : ℤ) ^ (5 * k + 1) * |N| ≤ M then some false
  else none

noncomputable def Q {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) : ℕ :=
  sInf {t : ℕ | QLe f t}

/-- Randomized query complexity. `sInf ∅ = 0` in `ℕ`, so every lower bound is
proved through `RLe` and the read-all witness that makes this set nonempty. -/
noncomputable def R {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : PartialBool ι) : ℕ :=
  sInf {t : ℕ | RLe f t}

/-- Finite classical control over unitary steps, oracle calls and binary
projective measurements. Computation between queries is unrestricted. -/
inductive AdaptiveProgram (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (w : ℕ) where
  | output (answer : Bool)
  | unitary (U : State ι w →ₗᵢ[ℂ] State ι w) (next : AdaptiveProgram ι w)
  | query (next : AdaptiveProgram ι w)
  | measure (S : Finset (Basis ι w)) (yes no : AdaptiveProgram ι w)

/-- `α_tot`, equation (1). -/
noncomputable def alphaTot : ℝ := sInf {α : ℝ | UniversalPower α}

structure Gate (ι : Type) (earlier : ℕ) where
  left : Option (ι ⊕ Fin earlier)
  right : Option (ι ⊕ Fin earlier)
  table : Bool → Bool → Bool

structure Circuit (ι : Type) where
  size : ℕ
  gate : (g : Fin size) → Gate ι g.val
  domainOut : Fin size
  valueOut : Fin size

/-- `O_x |i, b, z⟩ = |i, b ⊕ x_i, z⟩`. The oracle is an involution, so
permuting amplitudes by it is the same as permuting basis vectors by it. -/
noncomputable def bitOracle {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {w : ℕ}
    (x : BitInput ι) (ψ : State ι w) : State ι w :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun p =>
    ψ.ofLp (p.1, (if x p.1 then !p.2.1 else p.2.1), p.2.2)

/-- A finite mixture of decision trees. Every tree in the mixture has positive
probability, so worst-case depth below is over the support. -/
structure RandomizedProgram (ι : Type) where
  size : ℕ
  weight : Fin size → ℝ
  tree : Fin size → QueryTree ι
  weight_pos : ∀ j, 0 < weight j
  weight_sum : ∑ j, weight j = 1

def RandomizedProgram.depth {ι : Type} (A : RandomizedProgram ι) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup fun j => (A.tree j).depth

noncomputable def RandomizedProgram.success {ι : Type}
    (A : RandomizedProgram ι) (x : BitInput ι) (b : Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j, if (A.tree j).eval x = b then A.weight j else 0

inductive QueryTree (ι : Type) where
  | leaf (answer : Bool)
  | query (index : ι) (onFalse onTrue : QueryTree ι)

def QueryTree.eval {ι : Type} : QueryTree ι → BitInput ι → Bool
  | .leaf b, _ => b
  | .query i l r, x => if x i then r.eval x else l.eval x

/-- The longest root-to-leaf path. Repeated queries are charged. -/
def QueryTree.depth {ι : Type} : QueryTree ι → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 0
  | .query _ l r => 1 + max l.depth r.depth
